content.headline: Staff engineer for data platforms, from the first prototype to the service other teams depend on
content.summary: Staff engineer who takes data platforms from a first prototype to a dependable service. Designs the contracts between teams, writes the code that enforces them, and measures what users actually feel. Comfortable in front of clients, in a design review and in the middle of an incident, and happiest when a manual process disappears for good.
highlights: Turned a weekly manual export into a live service
Ran design reviews across four product teams
Wrote the evaluation suite that gates each release

bullets: Designed the event platform that carries orders, invoices and shipments between the sales, finance and logistics systems, with schemas checked at the edge and replay from any point in time.
Took the pricing engine from a spreadsheet maintained by hand to a typed service with its own test data, release notes and a dashboard the finance team reads every morning.
Introduced contract tests between the eight services of the order flow, so a breaking change fails in review rather than in production on a Friday evening.
Wrote and ran the evaluation suite that gates every release of the matching model, comparing precision and recall against a frozen reference set before anything ships.
Led the migration of the reporting warehouse to columnar storage, rehearsed on copies of production, with a rollback plan that was tested and never needed.
Scoped three client projects with the account team, turning loose wishes into written acceptance lines and a delivery plan the client signed.
Mentored four engineers through their first on call rotation, pairing on real incidents and writing down what each one taught us.
Built the internal command line tool that creates a new service with logging, metrics, health checks and a deploy pipeline in one step.
Ran the quarterly reliability review with every product team, turning each incident into one change of process and one test that would have caught it.
Moved the nightly batch of the billing reports to an incremental pipeline that finishes before the first team arrives, and wrote the runbook the on call engineer follows when it does not.
Built the ingestion layer for sensor data, from the devices to the time series store.
Wrote the alerting rules that page only when a customer would notice.
Maintained the shared libraries for configuration, logging and retries.
Ran the weekly architecture review and kept its decision log.
Automated the yearly certificate rotation across every environment.
Reduced the build time of the main repository by caching its dependencies.
Wrote the onboarding guide that new engineers follow in their first week, from a laptop with nothing on it to a change merged and deployed.
Paired with the support team every Friday to read the week's tickets and fix the three most common causes before the next release.
Wrote a test harness for the factory floor data collectors.
Documented the line controllers' message formats.
Prototyped a dashboard for the quality team.
Documented the test bench so that the next intern could run it alone on the first day.
Measured the bench against the reference instrument and wrote down every difference with its cause.

content.notes: Too long on purpose: it needs the tightest step, or overflows.
